objective: Development-only search for a better-forecasting world model on real HAI telemetry, measured by multi-step MAE (robust-scaled) on held-out NORMAL validation (HAI train5-6 after fitting on train1-4). No attack/test data read. Lower is better.
method: scripts/real_telemetry_world_model_exploration (real_telemetry_wm_explore.py). Reuses the registered real_telemetry_core.Forecaster (ridge + per-horizon LightGBM residual corrections, action-conditioned) with varied history length and boosting size; adds a small MLP and a per-horizon-history model as alternative technologies. Validation evaluated on a fixed seeded 40k-index subsample per horizon; fit rows subsampled per run (30k-50k) for speed. Baseline is the rt1/rt2 selected model (history 3, 60-tree GBR).

selected_improved_config.name: gbr_big_h12
selected_improved_config.description: ridge + LightGBM residuals (200 estimators, 63 leaves, lr 0.05, colsample 0.8, subsample 0.8), action-conditioned, history length 12
selected_improved_config.rationale: History length is the dominant lever; the 5-step gain plateaus at ~history 12 (see knee), so h12 captures nearly all the benefit at lower compute/inference cost than h16/h20.

findings: Temporal history length is the dominant lever for 5-step forecasting. H5 MAE improves monotonically: history 3 -> 5 -> 8 -> 12 gives roughly +0%, +3%, +7%, +9-10% over the baseline.
The 5-step gain plateaus at ~history 12 (h12 +9.9%, h16 +10.2%, h20 +10.3%). 1-step keeps improving slowly with more history (h12 +1.8% -> h20 +3.9%).
Nonlinearity is required to exploit the longer context: a longer-context LINEAR (ridge, history 8) was WORSE than the baseline (-4.6% H5). Gradient boosting on the same features captures the gain.
A small MLP (new technology) was clearly worse than gradient boosting (-12% to -18% H5). Not adopted.
A robust Huber boosting objective adds a little (gbr_huber_h8 +7.2% vs gbr_big_h8 +6.7% H5).
A per-horizon-history model (short history for H1, long for H5) balances both horizons but does not beat history-12 everywhere; history-12 improves both H1 and H5.
caveats: Measured on held-out NORMAL validation, not on attacks. A better normal-data forecaster gives tighter residuals and plausibly better attack detection, but any detection improvement must be confirmed on a FRESH registered split: the HAI 22.04/21.03/23.05 test attacks were already opened in rt1/rt2 and are spent for a clean final.
Model selection here is on the same validation that is reported, so the absolute numbers carry mild optimism; the relative ranking is robust across three rounds and fit sizes.
Longer history enlarges the feature vector, so inference cost and memory grow with history length; history 12 is the recommended compute/accuracy balance.
The registered rt1/rt2 world models are frozen and were NOT retrained; this is a forward-looking development result, not a change to any published result.
reproduce:
python scripts/real_telemetry_wm_explore.py 50000            (round 1)
python scripts/real_telemetry_wm_explore.py 40000 round2     (per-horizon / huber)
python scripts/real_telemetry_wm_explore.py 30000 round3     (history knee)
